When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue

Yen-Ju Lu*    Yuzhe Wang*    Yaohan Guan    Xiluo He    Jiarui Hai Affiliation: Mingrui Liang, Kaavya Chaparala, Thomas Thebaud, Affiliation: Laureano Moro-Velazquez, Najim Dehak, Jesus Villalba Affiliation: Center for Language and Speech Processing, Johns Hopkins University
Abstract

Understanding spoken dialogue requires joint reasoning over lexical content and paralinguistic acoustic signals such as emotion and conversational intent. However, existing evaluations often allow shortcuts based on transcripts or single-modality solutions, obscuring whether models genuinely ground predictions in speech. We formalize this failure mode as cross-modal disagreement, where transcripts suggest plausible but incorrect surface interpretations while acoustic cues such as prosody or speaking style support different answers. We develop a scalable framework that identifies text-biased surface interpretations and converts disagreement regions into conflict QA examples. We also include consistent cases where transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations agree, enabling evaluation beyond adversarial audio dependence. This results in ContraTalk, a controlled benchmark containing 501 questions across five discourse dimensions: interaction behavior, emotion state, dialogue act, social stance, and conversational intent. We further develop an agentic-style reasoning framework that converts speech into an Audio Twin, a text-readable representation of localized acoustic cues that exposes acoustic evidence to the reasoning model. Experiments show that strong text-only LLMs exceed 90% accuracy in consistent cases but drop to 33–48% in conflict cases. Direct AudioLLMs provide only partial grounding, still selecting the transcript-biased trap in roughly 30–40% of conflict cases. Our Audio Twin framework improves conflict-case accuracy while reducing trap selection, but its consistent-case behavior remains backbone-dependent. These results identify transcript-based shortcuts as an important failure mode in spoken dialogue understanding and show that explicit acoustic evidence aggregation provides a more controllable interface for diagnosing and improving speech-grounded reasoning.

1 Introduction

††footnotetext: ∗ denotes equal contribution.

Multimodal understanding is often framed as a problem of integrating complementary signals. In spoken dialogue, transcripts convey lexical and semantic cues, while acoustic cues from the audio reveal interaction behavior, emotion state, social stance, and conversational intent. Yet these modalities do not always align: speakers may sound hesitant while making confident statements, suppress frustration beneath polite wording, or signal intent through timing and delivery patterns that are not recoverable from text alone. Such cases introduce a distinct reasoning challenge: resolving not only what is said, but how it is said.

Despite rapid progress in multimodal modeling, many evaluation settings still permit modality shortcuts. This issue has been widely observed in visual question answering, where models exploit language priors rather than genuine visual grounding (Goyal et al., 2017), and in conversational emotion recognition, where textual features often dominate acoustic cues (Poria et al., 2019). Recent audio-language studies similarly show that strong performance can arise from lexical shortcuts or dataset-specific priors without genuine acoustic grounding (Yang et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2024a, e.g.,). More generally, when a benchmark can be solved from only one modality, the other modality becomes functionally ignorable. This creates a form of modality collapse: models may rely on transcripts when audio is needed, or rely on isolated audio cues without reasoning over dialogue context. A meaningful benchmark for spoken multimodal reasoning should therefore test whether models can compare, reconcile, and correct interpretations across modalities. We argue that cross-modal disagreement provides a distinct and underexplored axis for such evaluation.

To operationalize this perspective, we develop a scalable benchmark construction framework that starts from text-only surface interpretations, identifies regions where transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations diverge, and converts them into controlled question-answering instances. The resulting benchmark, ContraTalk, evaluates grounded spoken dialogue reasoning across five discourse-level dimensions: interaction behavior, emotion state, social stance, dialogue act, and conversational intent. Rather than focusing only on conflict cases, ContraTalk also includes consistent cases where transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations agree, enabling controlled evaluation of whether models use the appropriate evidence rather than collapsing to a single dominant modality.

Resolving such disagreement requires more than implicit multimodal fusion. A model must determine whether transcript-based reasoning is sufficient, identify which acoustic evidence is relevant, and compare competing interpretations when text and audio diverge. To support this process, we introduce Audio Twin, a structured, text-readable representation of localized acoustic and interactional evidence. Audio Twin converts speech-derived cues such as prosody, affect, timing, and speaking behavior into evidence that can be retrieved and compared with transcript-based interpretations during reasoning. This provides an explicit interface for spoken dialogue understanding: rather than treating audio as opaque input, the reasoning model receives speech-grounded evidence in a form that can be inspected and used to revise or confirm the surface interpretation suggested by the transcript.

Experiments show that strong text-only LLMs perform well on consistent cases but degrade substantially under cross-modal disagreement, revealing the limits of transcript-centric reasoning. Direct Audio-LLMs reduce some transcript-biased errors but still frequently select text-biased traps, indicating that audio access alone does not ensure speech grounding. Our Audio Twin framework further improves conflict-case accuracy and reduces trap selection, suggesting that explicit acoustic evidence aggregation can provide a more controllable interface for spoken dialogue reasoning.

Our contributions are threefold:

  • •

    We identify transcript-based shortcuts under cross-modal disagreement as an important failure mode in spoken dialogue understanding, and formalize this setting as requiring models to reconcile lexical and paralinguistic evidence.

  • •

    We introduce ContraTalk, a controlled spoken dialogue QA benchmark constructed from text–audio disagreement regions, together with consistent cases that test whether models preserve transcript-supported reasoning when modalities agree.

  • •

    We develop an agentic-style Audio Twin reasoning framework that converts localized speech-derived cues into text-readable evidence for reconciling transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations.

2 Related Work

Modality Bias and Shortcut Learning. Multimodal learning has long been challenged by representation imbalance, where models disproportionately rely on a dominant modality while underutilizing others (Wang et al., 2020). This phenomenon is closely related to shortcut learning (Geirhos et al., 2020), in which neural networks exploit easy-to-learn priors rather than integrating complex multimodal evidence. In spoken dialogue and emotion recognition, modality bias is particularly pronounced: textual transcripts often provide highly predictive semantic shortcuts, causing models to favor lexical cues while marginalizing paralinguistic and acoustic signals (Poria et al., 2019; Wagner et al., 2023). This imbalance is especially consequential in conversational settings, where meaning frequently emerges from pragmatic and affective cues expressed through prosody, timing, and interaction dynamics rather than lexical content alone. Although prior work has proposed debiasing strategies and regularization techniques (Wu et al., 2022), existing evaluation paradigms rarely place models in scenarios where resolving explicit cross-modal disagreement is necessary for successful reasoning.

Multimodal Reasoning and Evaluation for Audio-LLMs. The rapid development of Audio-LLMs has shifted spoken dialogue understanding toward unified end-to-end modeling paradigms, increasing the need for rigorous evaluation of multimodal reasoning capabilities (Tang et al., 2024; Chu et al., 2023). In parallel, the community has introduced diverse benchmarks for audio-language understanding, compositional reasoning, instruction following, and conversational interaction, including AIR-Bench, AudioBench, and MMAU (Yang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025; Sakshi et al., ). Prior work has also explored modality-interaction phenomena such as multimodal sarcasm (Castro et al., 2019) and semantic meaning shifts in image–text pairs (Kiela et al., 2020). However, these benchmarks largely evaluate settings where modalities are cooperative, complementary, or independently informative. In contrast, ContraTalk targets cross-modal disagreement in spoken dialogue, where transcript-based interpretations can be plausible but wrong, and acoustic or interactional evidence is required to correct, refine, or disambiguate them.

Agentic-style Multimodal Reasoning To handle complex multimodal inputs, recent approaches have adopted reasoning-and-acting paradigms that decompose problems and leverage external tools (Yao et al., 2023; Schick et al., 2023). This trend has led to multimodal orchestration frameworks in which a central language model dynamically routes queries to specialized perceptual modules or engages in iterative retrieval loops to gather relevant context (Shen et al., 2023; Huang et al., 2024b). More recent work also uses structured digital-twin representations to expose perceptual states to LLM-based reasoning systems; for example, Shen et al. (2025) construct an operating-room digital twin that preserves semantic and spatial relationships and supports a reason-retrieve-synthesize workflow for reasoning segmentation. Our Audio Twin follows this broader direction of making perceptual evidence explicit and LLM-readable, but shifts the focus from complementary evidence retrieval to cross-modal evidence arbitration. Rather than assuming retrieved evidence is mutually consistent with the text query, our framework explicitly resolves epistemic disagreement between transcript-derived interpretations and acoustic signals.

3 Inconsistent-Aware Multimodal Reasoning

3.1 Problem Formulation

We study spoken dialogue understanding as inference over paired textual and acoustic evidence. A dialogue instance is represented as D=(T,A),D=(T,A), where TT denotes the transcript and AA denotes the corresponding audio. The transcript primarily conveys lexical content, while the acoustic signal provides paralinguistic and interactional cues such as prosody and affect. We define Cross-modal disagreement reasoning as the setting where models must explicitly detect, interpret, and resolve conflicting evidence across modalities, rather than assuming alignment or relying on a single dominant modality. The goal is to evaluate whether models can use audio when it materially affects interpretation while remaining calibrated when the transcript and audio are aligned. We formulate the task as multiple-choice question answering over spoken dialogue. Given a dialogue instance (T,A)(T,A), a question qq, and answer candidates 𝒞={c1,…,cK}\mathcal{C}=\{c_{1},\dots,c_{K}\}, we distinguish between two inference views:

y^T=fT​(T,q,𝒞),y^T​A=fT​A​(T,A,q,𝒞).\hat{y}_{T}=f_{T}(T,q,\mathcal{C}),\qquad\hat{y}_{TA}=f_{TA}(T,A,q,\mathcal{C}).

Here, y^T\hat{y}_{T} denotes the answer induced by transcript-only reasoning, and y^T​A\hat{y}_{TA} denotes the answer supported by the full spoken dialogue, including acoustic evidence. We define two evaluation regimes:

conflict: y^T≠y^T​A,y⋆=y^T​A,consistent: y^T=y^T​A=y⋆.\text{conflict: }\hat{y}_{T}\neq\hat{y}_{TA},\;y^{\star}=\hat{y}_{TA},\qquad\text{consistent: }\hat{y}_{T}=\hat{y}_{TA}=y^{\star}.

In conflict instances, the transcript induces a plausible but incorrect surface answer, while acoustic evidence determines the gold answer. In consistent instances, both modalities support the same answer, testing whether models remain calibrated when no cross-modal correction is required. Each question targets a discourse-level interpretation, such as interaction behavior, emotion state, social stance, dialogue act, or conversational intent.

3.2 ContraTalk Benchmark Construction

Data source and construction-time signals. We construct ContraTalk from the Seamless Interaction Dataset (Agrawal et al., 2025), which provides spoken dialogues, transcripts, and speaker prompts describing intended speaker states, roles, or communicative behaviors. We use these prompts only as construction-time signals to propose candidate audio-grounded interpretations and candidate answer options. They are not provided to models during evaluation.

Construction overview. The goal of the construction process is to create multiple-choice QA instances that evaluate two complementary settings: cases where speech evidence should correct a transcript-based interpretation, and cases where the transcript-supported interpretation should be preserved. As summarized in Figure 2, we first derive transcript-based surface interpretations and speaker-conditioned audio-grounded interpretations, then construct examples based on their relationship. In the conflict split, these two interpretations differ: the transcript supports a plausible but incorrect surface interpretation, while acoustic or interactional evidence supports a different grounded answer. We therefore include the transcript-based interpretation as a text-biased distractor, allowing us to measure whether models are misled by transcript-only reasoning. In the consistent split, the transcript-based and speech-grounded interpretations agree. Since the surface interpretation matches the grounded answer, no separate misleading option is defined for this split; consistent cases are evaluated by accuracy only. All instances are verified through automatic checks and targeted human review to ensure that the final answer is supported by the available evidence and that answer choices are distinct. Full details of the construction pipeline, including conflict/consistent region selection, question generation, QA-only leakage filtering, and automatic revision are provided in Appendix B.

Benchmark composition. Because the labeled Seamless Interaction test split contains 117 spoken dialogues, ContraTalk uses all available test dialogues and derives 501 multiple-choice questions from them. The questions cover five discourse-level dimensions: interaction behavior, emotion state, social stance, dialogue act, and conversational intent. The benchmark includes both conflict cases, where acoustic or interactional cues are needed to resolve cross-modal disagreement, and consistent cases, where the transcript-supported interpretation should be preserved. Table 1 summarizes the distribution across discourse dimensions.

Human verification. We perform targeted human verification through model-disagreement review and sampling-based quality control. Each candidate instance is evaluated by complementary systems, including a direct Audio-LLM and our agentic-style Audio Twin system; disagreement cases are prioritized for manual review, while agreement cases are sampled for auditing. In total, 350 of the 501 final examples are manually reviewed by seven reviewers, who listen to the audio and inspect the transcript, question, answer choices, and final answer while remaining blind to the speaker prompts. Reviewers verify audio grounding, transcript-only distractor plausibility, and answer-option distinctiveness. Flagged cases are revised, removed, or collected for a unified second-pass review. The verification protocol and full evaluator instructions are provided in Appendices D and E.

4 Agentic-style Inference with Audio Twin

We introduce an agentic-style framework that augments the lexical transcript with a transcript-aligned Audio Twin, making speech-derived evidence explicit and available for comparison with transcript-based interpretations before answer selection.

4.1 Overview

Building on the QA formulation in Section 3, our pipeline performs audio-grounded inference in two steps. It first constructs an Audio Twin, a transcript-aligned evidence structure that links text-readable speech cues to dialogue turns and speakers. Given a question, it then retrieves relevant Audio Twin evidence and conditions answer prediction on both the transcript and retrieved speech-derived evidence. Given a transcript TT, Audio Twin evidence EATE_{\mathrm{AT}}, question qq, and answer candidates 𝒞\mathcal{C}, the retrieval module returns question-relevant evidence Eq⊆EATE_{q}\subseteq E_{\mathrm{AT}}. The final answer is predicted as

y^=f⁡(T,Eq,q,𝒞).\hat{y}=f(T,E_{q},q,\mathcal{C}).

Here, EqE_{q} is not generic external context, but transcript-aligned acoustic evidence for comparing lexical and speech-grounded interpretations. It exposes paralinguistic cues in a text-readable form, allowing the reasoning model to condition on both what was said and how it was said. This distinction is central to ContraTalk: the transcript may support a plausible surface answer, while the correct answer requires grounding in acoustic evidence.

4.2 Audio Twin Representation

We instantiate the Audio Twin as a structured, text-readable representation of a spoken dialogue. Given a dialogue D=(T,A)D=(T,A), where TT is the timestamped transcript and AA is the corresponding audio, speech front ends extract acoustic and paralinguistic features FF and align them to transcript turns. An Audio Twin builder converts the transcript and aligned speech features into a question-independent evidence structure:

EAT=ϕAT​(T,F),E_{\mathrm{AT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{AT}}(T,F),

where EATE_{\mathrm{AT}} denotes the structured evidence used for downstream retrieval and reasoning.

The core goal of Audio Twin is to avoid modality collapse: rather than allowing the reasoning model to default to the transcript or treat audio as an opaque input, Audio Twin exposes speech delivery as explicit evidence that can be compared against transcript-based interpretations. It represents prosodic, affective, fluency, timing, and overlap cues as compact textual evidence linked to dialogue turns and speakers. When speaker normalization is meaningful, cues are expressed relative to speaker-specific baselines, allowing the model to reason about whether a speaker sounds louder, faster, or more hesitant than usual. Implementation details, including evidence-card fields, alignment reliability, and feature textualization, are provided in Appendix F.

4.3 Agentic-style Evidence Retrieval

Given a question qq and the target discourse dimension, the retrieval module constructs an evidence plan that specifies what speech-grounded evidence should be retrieved before answer prediction. The plan defines the needed evidence types, while a transcript locator identifies the dialogue turns that should serve as anchors. Inference proceeds in three stages. First, the transcript locator selects a small set of relevant transcript anchors without choosing an answer. Second, the retrieval module uses these anchors and the evidence plan to fetch the corresponding Audio Twin evidence, including aligned turn-level evidence, speaker baselines, local context, and interaction-level summaries when needed. Third, the reasoning model compares transcript-based interpretations with the retrieved speech-grounded evidence and selects the answer most directly supported by the evidence bundle. For retrieval, let U={ui}i=1NU=\{u_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N} denote the set of transcript turns induced by transcript TT, and let πq\pi_{q} denote the question-conditioned evidence plan. The plan selects relevant transcript anchors

Sq=πq​(U,q),Sq⊆U.S_{q}=\pi_{q}(U,q),\qquad S_{q}\subseteq U.

The retrieval module then returns question-relevant Audio Twin evidence, which is used for answer prediction:

Eq=ℛ⁡(EAT,Sq,πq),y^=f⁡(T,Eq,q,𝒞).E_{q}=\mathcal{R}(E_{\mathrm{AT}},S_{q},\pi_{q}),\qquad\hat{y}=f(T,E_{q},q,\mathcal{C}).

Here, EqE_{q} contains the Audio Twin entries aligned to the selected anchors, while TT provides the full lexical context. Details are provided in Appendix G.

5 Experiments

We organize our evaluation around three research questions:

RQ1: Does ContraTalk expose transcript shortcuts on conflict cases? We test whether transcript-only models are misled when acoustic evidence is needed to resolve cross-modal conflict.

RQ2: Do models preserve performance on consistent cases? We test whether audio-capable or agentic-style systems preserve transcript-supported answers when no cross-modal correction is needed.

RQ3: How does audio grounding change model behavior? We compare text-only inference, direct audio inference, and Audio Twin reasoning across both splits to analyze grounding gains and new failure modes.

5.1 Experimental Setup

Evaluation protocol. Each ContraTalk instance consists of dialogue audio AA, transcript TT, question qq, and answer candidates 𝒞={c1,…,cK}\mathcal{C}=\{c_{1},\ldots,c_{K}\}.

Models. We evaluate text-only LLMs, Audio-LLMs, and Audio Twin systems, covering transcript-only inference, direct speech inference, and structured acoustic-evidence reasoning. When possible, we compare matched text-only and audio-capable variants to isolate the effect of modality access. Full model details are provided in Appendix H.

Metrics. We report accuracy and mislead rate. Accuracy measures whether the model selects the gold answer. Mislead rate measures selection of the text-biased surface distractor and is reported for conflict cases, where such a distractor is defined. For consistent cases, we report accuracy. Metrics are reported overall and by discourse-level category. We report dialogue-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals in Appendix C.

5.2 Experimental Results

RQ1: Does ContraTalk expose transcript shortcuts on conflict cases? We first evaluate whether the conflict split of ContraTalk exposes transcript-based shortcut behavior. Table 2 reports category-wise accuracy and mislead rate on cases where the transcript supports a plausible surface interpretation, while speech-grounded evidence supports a different answer. Text-only LLMs perform modestly on conflict cases but frequently select the transcript-biased distractor. Overall, they obtain 33.0–47.7% accuracy while choosing the mislead option in 34.5–45.0% of examples. The shortcut is especially visible for emotion state and conversational intent, where several text-only models show mislead rates above 40%. This indicates that the conflict split exposes a systematic shortcut: the transcript alone supports a plausible but incorrect interpretation that can compete with the speech-grounded answer. Direct Audio-LLMs only partially reduce this failure mode. Their accuracy ranges from 33.6% to 46.8%, while mislead rates remain high at 29.7–39.9%, indicating that raw audio access alone does not guarantee grounding when transcript and speech cues disagree. Audio Twin reasoning provides the strongest overall shortcut resistance among the evaluated systems. Across LLM backbones, Audio Twin variants reach 43.2–50.5% accuracy with 29.4–34.8% mislead rate. Sonnet 4.5 with Audio Twin achieves the best overall accuracy and lowest overall mislead rate, with strong category-level performance on conversational intent and dialogue act. Nevertheless, the remaining misled cases show that Audio Twin reasoning mitigates, but does not eliminate, transcript-induced shortcuts. Overall, the conflict split exposes a targeted cross-modal failure mode: models may prefer transcript-plausible answers even when they conflict with how the dialogue is spoken.

RQ2: Do models preserve performance on consistent cases? We next evaluate whether models remain reliable on consistent cases, where transcript-supported and speech-grounded interpretations agree. Table 3 reports category-wise accuracy. Because no text-biased surface distractor is defined, we report accuracy only. Models perform substantially better on consistent cases than on conflict cases. Strong text-only LLMs often exceed 90% accuracy, with Opus 4.7 reaching 98.2% overall. Their performance is especially high on conversational intent and dialogue act, where the strongest text-only models reach 100% accuracy. This suggests that ContraTalk不仅仅是由于含糊的问题或嘈杂的选择而变得困难；当文字记录和语音提示出现分歧时，就会出现主要的挑战。 直接音频 LLM 在许多一致的示例上实现了高精度，但它们的性能在不同系统中不太统一。 例如，StepAudio-R1 整体达到 89.9%，而 StepAudio-2 则下降至 69.6%。 对于较弱的音频法学硕士，这种下降在交互行为和对话行为中尤其明显，这表明语音访问并不总是保留转录支持的解释。 音频孪生推理显示了类似的主干依赖模式：Opus 4.7 + AT 保持了 94.0% 的强大、一致的情况准确率，而较小的主干性能下降更多。 与冲突分裂结果一起，该比较表明is not simply difficult due to ambiguous questions or noisy choices; the main challenge arises when transcript and speech cues diverge. Direct Audio-LLMs achieve high accuracy on many consistent examples, but their performance is less uniform across systems. For example, StepAudio-R1 reaches 89.9% overall, while StepAudio-2 drops to 69.6%. The drop is particularly visible in interaction behavior and dialogue acts for weaker Audio-LLMs, suggesting that speech access does not always preserve transcript-supported interpretations. Audio Twin reasoning shows a similar backbone-dependent pattern: Opus 4.7 + AT maintains strong, consistent-case accuracy at 94.0%, whereas smaller backbones degrade more. Together with the conflict-split results, this comparison shows that对话ContraTalk区分两种行为：当模式一致时保留正确的解释，当它们冲突时修改基于记录的解释。separates two behaviors: preserving correct interpretations when modalities agree, and revising transcript-based interpretations when they conflict.

This paired view allows us to examine whether adding speech helps resolve transcript-based shortcuts on conflict cases without disrupting transcript-supported reasoning on consistent cases. The paired comparison reveals a modality-collapse pattern. Several direct Audio-LLMs improve conflict-case behavior, either increasing conflict accuracy or reducing mislead rate, but their accuracy drops on the consistent split after speech is introduced. This suggests that speech input can shift model predictions away from transcript-biased shortcuts, but may also destabilize cases where the transcript already supports the correct answer. Other Audio-LLMs show limited improvement on conflict cases and similar mislead rates, suggesting continued reliance on transcript-based cues despite audio input. Thus, direct audio access does not guarantee calibrated multimodal reasoning, either improving conflict cases at the cost of consistency or showing limited corrective use of audio. Our Audio Twin framework improves conflict-case accuracy while reducing trap selection, but its consistent-case behavior remains backbone-dependent: smaller backbones are more easily perturbed by added acoustic evidence, while stronger backbones better preserve transcript-supported predictions. Overall, effective speech grounding should correct transcript-based shortcuts under conflict while preserving transcript-supported reasoning when modalities agree.

6 结论Conclusion

我们介绍了We introduced对话ContraTalk，评估跨模式分歧下口语对话理解的基准。与仅通过文字记录或仅通过音频即可解决的评估不同，, a benchmark for evaluating spoken dialogue understanding under cross-modal disagreement. Unlike evaluations that can be solved from transcripts alone or from audio alone,对话ContraTalk将冲突案例与一致案例区分开来，在冲突案例中，基于文字记录的解释是合理的，但与声学证据相矛盾，在一致案例中，文字记录和语音支持相同的答案。这种设计使我们不仅可以测试模型是否可以使用音频来纠正转录快捷方式，还可以测试模型在不需要纠正时是否保持校准状态。separates conflict cases, where transcript-based interpretations are plausible but contradicted by acoustic evidence, from consistent cases, where transcript and speech support the same answer. This design enables us to test not only whether models can use audio to correct transcript shortcuts, but also whether they remain calibrated when no correction is needed.

我们的实验表明，强大的纯文本法学硕士在一致的情况下表现良好，但在冲突的情况下急剧下降，证实基于转录的性能可以掩盖基于语音的理解中的失败。直接音频LLM仅提供部分基础：语音输入有时会提高冲突情况的准确性，但误导率仍然很高，并且当引入音频时，一致情况的准确性可能会下降。我们的代理式音频孪生框架为声学证据提供了更明确的接口，并改善了多个骨干网的冲突情况行为。同时，一致情况的结果表明，必须选择性地而不是统一地应用显式音频接地。Our experiments show that strong text-only LLMs perform well on consistent cases but degrade sharply on conflict cases, confirming that transcript-based performance can mask failures in speech-grounded understanding. Direct AudioLLMs provide only partial grounding: speech input sometimes improves conflict-case accuracy, but mislead rates remain substantial and consistent-case accuracy can drop when audio is introduced. Our agentic-style Audio Twin framework provides a more explicit interface to acoustic evidence and improves conflict-case behavior for several backbones. At the same time, the consistent-case results show that explicit audio grounding must be applied selectively rather than uniformly.

这些发现表明，强大的口语对话理解需要的不仅仅是隐式多模态融合，同时还强调必须有选择地使用显式声学证据。模型必须学会决定何时转录证据是可靠的，何时声音提示应该修改表面阅读，以及如何在不破坏其他正确的文本支持推理的情况下合并语音衍生的证据。我们希望These findings suggest that robust spoken dialogue understanding requires more than implicit multimodal fusion, while also highlighting that explicit acoustic evidence must be used selectively. Models must learn to decide when transcript evidence is reliable, when acoustic cues should revise a surface reading, and how to incorporate speech-derived evidence without disrupting otherwise correct text-supported reasoning. We hope对话ContraTalk支持未来在分歧感知评估、校准声学接地和推理架构方面的工作，使语音证据更加明确、可审计和可靠。supports future work on disagreement-aware evaluation, calibrated acoustic grounding, and reasoning architectures that make speech evidence more explicit, auditable, and reliable.

局限性Limitations

这项工作的重点是受控的跨模式分歧，而不是现实世界口语对话理解中的全方位线索。音频孪生是基于音频的显式推理的一种实例；附录中提供了进一步的讨论This work focuses on controlled cross-modal disagreement rather than the full range of cues in real-world spoken dialogue understanding. Audio Twin is one instantiation of explicit audio-grounded reasoning; further discussion is provided in AppendixA.

附录AAppendix A局限性Limitations

这项工作的重点是在受控的跨模式分歧下评估和减轻转录捷径，而不是提供口语对话理解的完整解决方案。虽然This work focuses on evaluating and mitigating transcript shortcuts under controlled cross-modal disagreement, rather than providing a complete solution to spoken dialogue understanding. Although对话ContraTalk尽管它涵盖了多个话语层面的维度，但它并没有穷尽可能塑造现实世界对话的全部声学、实用、社会和文化线索。covers multiple discourse-level dimensions, it does not exhaust the full range of acoustic, pragmatic, social, and cultural cues that may shape real-world conversations.

我们的音频孪生框架也只是显式音频推理的一种实例。更复杂的代理系统、更强大的语音编码器或改进的证据选择策略可能会进一步提高协调冲突模式的能力。Our Audio Twin framework is also only one instantiation of explicit audio-grounded reasoning. More complex agentic systems, stronger speech encoders, or improved evidence selection strategies may further improve the ability to reconcile conflicting modalities.

最后，音频孪生提供了一个可解释的声学证据接口，但其实用性取决于提取的语音提示的保真度。自动转录、对齐、韵律分析和情感线索估计可能会引入噪声，当相关证据微妙、模糊或难以定位时，这可能会限制推理性能。Finally, Audio Twin provides an interpretable interface to acoustic evidence, but its utility depends on the fidelity of the extracted speech cues. Automatic transcription, alignment, prosodic analysis, and affective cue estimation may introduce noise, which can limit reasoning performance when the relevant evidence is subtle, ambiguous, or difficult to localize.

附录BAppendix BContraTalk 基准建设细节ContraTalk Benchmark Construction Details

本附录提供了完整的构建和验证程序This appendix provides the full construction and verification procedure for对话ContraTalk。 主要论文在第 5 节中总结了总体流程. The main paper summarizes the overall pipeline in Section3.2;在这里我们详细描述每个步骤。概览如图所示。; here we describe each step in detail. The overview is shown in Fig.4

第 1 步：纯文本表面解释。Step 1: Text-only surface interpretation.

我们首先估计纯文本推理机仅从文字记录中形成的解释。 给定对话记录，我们提示语言模型沿着五个话语级别维度对话语进行注释：We first estimate the interpretation that a text-only reasoner would form from the transcript alone. Given a dialogue transcript, we prompt a language model to annotate utterances along five discourse-level dimensions:互动行为、情绪状态、社会立场、对话行为interaction behavior, emotion state, social stance, dialogue act, 和, and会话意图conversational intent。 此步骤捕获转录引起的表面偏差，并作为识别文本音频分歧的比较点。. This step captures transcript-induced surface bias and serves as the comparison point for identifying text–audio disagreement.

第 2 步：扬声器条件标签比较。Step 2: Speaker-conditioned label comparison.

我们将纯文本的表面解释与从数据集提示中派生的、以说话者为条件的候选接地标签进行比较。 这些提示仅用作构建时信号来建议候选音频接地标签；它们在评估过程中不会提供给模型，最终标签是在人工验证后分配的。 该比较产生两种类型的候选区域。 首先，我们确定We compare the text-only surface interpretations with speaker-conditioned candidate grounded labels derived from the dataset prompts. The prompts are used only as construction-time signals to propose candidate audio-grounded labels; they are not provided to models during evaluation, and final labels are assigned after human verification. This comparison produces two types of candidate regions. First, we identify冲突conflict基于转录的解释与预期的口头实现不一致、未明确说明或具有误导性的区域。 其次，我们确定regions where the transcript-based interpretation is inconsistent with, underspecified relative to, or misleading compared with the intended spoken realization. Second, we identify一致的consistent基于转录的解释与说话者条件接地标签密切相关的区域。 前者支持构建依赖于音频的冲突问题，而后者支持构建文本可解决的一致问题。regions where the transcript-based interpretation is closely aligned with the speaker-conditioned grounded label. The former supports construction of audio-dependent conflict questions, while the latter supports construction of text-solvable consistent questions.

第三步：产生冲突和一致的问题。Step 3: Conflict and consistent question generation.

我们将选定的区域转换为两种制度下的多项选择 QA 实例。 对于冲突案例，每个问题都针对话语层面的维度，并要求对话语或对话片段进行有根据的解释。 正确答案反映了预期的口头实现，而文本偏向的干扰项旨在在仅记录的推理下保持合理性。 这使得错误选项成为结构化陷阱，而不是随机否定。 对于一致的情况，我们从基于转录和说话人条件的解释一致的区域生成问题。 正确答案得到文字记录和口语实现的支持，并且干扰因素被构造为可以清楚地区分，而不依赖于跨模式分歧。 这些一致的问题测试在不需要基于音频的校正时模型是否保留转录支持的解释。We convert the selected regions into multiple-choice QA instances under two regimes. For conflict cases, each question targets a discourse-level dimension and asks for the grounded interpretation of an utterance or dialogue segment. The correct answer reflects the intended spoken realization, while a text-biased distractor is designed to remain plausible under transcript-only reasoning. This makes the incorrect option a structured trap rather than a random negative. For consistent cases, we generate questions from regions where transcript-based and speaker-conditioned interpretations agree. The correct answer is supported by both the transcript and the spoken realization, and the distractors are constructed to be clearly distinguishable without relying on cross-modal disagreement. These consistent questions test whether models preserve transcript-supported interpretations when no audio-based correction is required.

第四步：自动质量控制。Step 4: Automatic quality control.

自动生成的问题可能包含无需对话证据即可揭示答案的工件。 因此，我们首先在仅 QA 的设置中运行每个实例，其中模型仅接收候选问题和答案，没有文字记录或音频，并被要求提供答案及其推理。 我们审核仅限 QA 的推理，以确定答案是否可以仅根据候选问答来证明是合理的。 如果推理揭示了有效的独立于对话的捷径，我们将重写问题并在第二轮中重新运行仅 QA 测试。 修改后在没有对话证据的情况下仍可负责的实例将被删除。Automatically generated questions may contain artifacts that reveal the answer without requiring dialogue evidence. We therefore first run each instance in a QA-only setting, where the model receives only the question and answer candidates, without transcript or audio, and is asked to provide both an answer and its reasoning. We audit the QA-only reasoning to determine whether the answer can be justified solely from the question and answer candidates. If the reasoning reveals a valid dialogue-independent shortcut, we rewrite the question and rerun the QA-only test in a second round. Instances that remain answerable without dialogue evidence after revision are removed.

第5步：人工验证。Step 5: Human verification.

最后，我们手动验证候选实例的可回答性、证据质量和干扰有效性。 对于冲突情况，我们优先使用两个自动验证器进行审查：直接音频 LLM 和音频双管道。 验证者不一致的案例被视为高风险案例并进行手动检查。 对于一致的情况，没有定义文本偏向的表面干扰项，我们改为进行基于随机采样的质量控制。 注释者聆听音频并修改或删除证据不明确、答案不明确或答案选择无法区分的实例。Finally, we manually verify candidate instances for answerability, evidence quality, and distractor validity. For conflict cases, we prioritize review using two automatic validators: a direct Audio-LLM and an Audio Twin pipeline. Validator-disagreement cases are treated as higher-risk cases and manually inspected. For consistent cases, where no text-biased surface distractor is defined, we instead conduct random sampling-based quality control. Annotators listen to the audio and revise or remove instances with unclear evidence, ambiguous answers, or indistinguishable answer choices.

附录CAppendix C统计不确定性Statistical Uncertainty

表Table5报告汇总了表 2-4 中使用的主要指标的置信区间。reports aggregate confidence intervals for the main metrics used in Tables 2–4.

我们使用非参数对话级引导程序来估计不确定性。 对于每个系统和评估分割，我们对对话进行替换采样，包括从每个采样对话中得出的所有问题，并重新计算准确性，对于冲突情况，重新计算误导率。 我们使用所得指标分布的第 2.5 个和 97.5 个百分位数报告了 10,000 个引导样本的 95% 百分位数置信区间。报告的区间是百分位数置信区间，而不是标准差或 标准错误，并且该过程不假设正态错误分布。We estimate uncertainty using a nonparametric dialogue-level bootstrap. For each system and evaluation split, we sample dialogues with replacement, include all questions derived from each sampled dialogue, and recompute accuracy and, for conflict cases, mislead rate. We report 95% percentile confidence intervals from 10,000 bootstrap samples, using the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the resulting metric distribution. The reported intervals are percentile confidence intervals, not standard deviations or standard errors, and the procedure does not assume a normal error distribution.

由于多个问题可能来自同一个对话，因此我们对对话而不是单个问题进行重新采样。 这些间隔量化了对话级重采样下的分数变异性Because multiple questions may come from the same dialogue, we resample dialogues rather than individual questions. These intervals quantify score variability under dialogue-level resampling of对话ContraTalk;它们没有考虑替代基准构建或标签决策的不确定性。; they do not account for uncertainty from alternative benchmark construction or labeling decisions.

附录DAppendix D人工验证协议Human Verification Protocol

我们使用的验证协议将冲突案例的针对性审查与一致案例的基于抽样的质量控制相结合。 在人工审查之前，每个冲突候选者都会通过补充系统进行评估，包括纯文本法学硕士、直接音频法学硕士和我们的代理式音频孪生推理系统。 系统不同意的情况将被视为高风险情况并进行人工审核。 对于一致的候选人，如果文字记录和语音证据支持相同的答案，并且没有定义文本偏向的表面干扰因素，我们会进行基于随机抽样的审查来检查整体质量。 总之，此过程会从最终 501 个示例中生成 350 个手动审核的实例。 表We use a verification protocol that combines targeted review for conflict cases with sampling-based quality control for consistent cases. Before human review, each conflict candidate is evaluated by complementary systems, including a text-only LLM, a direct Audio-LLM, and our agentic-style Audio Twin reasoning system. Instances for which the systems disagree are treated as higher-risk cases and manually reviewed. For consistent candidates, where the transcript and speech evidence support the same answer and no text-biased surface distractor is defined, we conduct random sampling-based review to check overall quality. Together, this procedure results in 350 manually reviewed instances out of the final 501 examples. Table6总结了验证范围和主要故障模式。summarizes the verification coverage and major failure modes.

人工验证由七名审核员进行。 审阅者会获得对话音频、文字记录、问题、答案选择和建议的最终答案，但对基准构建期间使用的构建时扬声器提示视而不见。 他们被指示聆听音频并验证所选答案是否得到对话证据的支持、答案选择是否足够明确以及问题是否可以在不依赖构建时元数据的情况下回答。 对于冲突案例，审阅者还会检查表面干扰因素是否仅从文字记录中看来是合理的，同时与基于语音的答案保持可区分性。Human verification is conducted by seven reviewers. Reviewers are given the dialogue audio, transcript, question, answer choices, and the proposed final answer, but are blind to the construction-time speaker prompts used during benchmark construction. They are instructed to listen to the audio and verify whether the selected answer is supported by the dialogue evidence, whether the answer choices are sufficiently distinct, and whether the question is answerable without relying on construction-time metadata. For conflict cases, reviewers additionally check whether the surface distractor is plausible from the transcript alone while remaining distinguishable from the speech-grounded answer.

如果音频证据不清楚、正确答案没有充分依据、选项不明确或干扰项与验证答案太接近，则实例将被修改或删除。 当审阅者不确定时，会收集实例进行第二轮验证，在统一准则下重新检查证据、答案选项和最终标签。 只有通过此过程的示例才会保留在最终基准中；否则，它们将被修改或丢弃。Instances are revised or removed if the audio evidence is unclear, the correct answer is not sufficiently grounded, the options are ambiguous, or the distractor is too close to the verified answer. When reviewers are uncertain, the instance is collected for a second-pass verification round, where the evidence, answer options, and final label are re-examined under a unified guideline. Only examples that pass this process are retained in the final benchmark; otherwise, they are revised or discarded.

附录EAppendix E给人类评估者的指示Instructions Given to Human Evaluators

本节提供了在验证过程中向人工评估人员显示的完整说明。This section provides the full instructions shown to human evaluators during verification.

任务描述。Task description.

每个实例包含一个问题、四个答案选项、一个带标签的答案索引、一段大约 15 秒的短音频片段以及供参考的文字记录。 评估人员被要求使用音频作为主要证据来源来验证标记的答案是否正确。 文字记录可以用作支持，但是当音频和文字记录提出不同的解释时，评估人员会被指示信任音频。Each instance contains a question, four answer choices, a labeled answer index, a short audio segment of approximately 15 seconds, and a transcript for reference. Evaluators are asked to verify whether the labeled answer is correct, using the audio as the primary source of evidence. The transcript may be used as support, but when the audio and transcript suggest different interpretations, evaluators are instructed to trust the audio.

验证任务。Verification task.

对于每个实例，评估人员首先收听音频并确定标记的答案是否正确。 如果标记的答案正确，他们会将实例标记为正确。 如果标记的答案不正确，他们会更新最终答案索引或修改答案选项之一。For each instance, evaluators first listen to the audio and decide whether the labeled answer is correct. If the labeled answer is correct, they mark the instance as correct. If the labeled answer is incorrect, they either update the final answer index or revise one of the answer choices.

当四个选项中已经存在正确答案时，评估人员只需更新最终答案索引即可。 如果四个选项均不完全正确，评估人员会修改其中一个选项并提供最终答案索引和更新的选项文本。 他们被要求保持答案选择清晰、具体且可相互区分，以便每个选项都表达独特的情感、意图、立场或行为。When the correct answer is already present among the four choices, evaluators simply update the final answer index. If none of the four choices is fully correct, evaluators revise one choice and provide both the final answer index and the updated choice text. They are instructed to keep answer choices clear, specific, and mutually distinguishable, so that each option expresses a distinct emotion, intent, stance, or behavior.

误导选项。Mislead options.

对于冲突情况，每个问题都包含一个误导选项，这是一个有意设计的文本偏向干扰项。 评估人员被告知不要仅仅因为它被标记为干扰因素而避免该选项。 如果音频实际上支持误导选项，他们应该通过更新答案索引来选择它作为最终答案。For conflict cases, each question includes a mislead option, which is an intentionally designed text-biased distractor. Evaluators are told not to avoid this option simply because it is labeled as a distractor. If the mislead option is actually supported by the audio, they should select it as the final answer by updating the answer index.

质量控制指南。Quality-control guidelines.

评估人员被要求优先考虑音频证据而不是基于文字记录的解释，避免做出几乎相同的两个答案选择，并确保最终选项保持清晰可辨。 当可以通过更改索引或编辑选项来更正答案时，实例就会被修改。 当音频证据不清楚、问题无法回答或选项不能足够清晰时，实例就会被删除。Evaluators are instructed to prioritize audio evidence over transcript-based interpretations, avoid making two answer choices nearly identical, and ensure that the final options remain clearly distinguishable. Instances are revised when the answer can be corrected by changing the index or editing a choice. Instances are removed when the audio evidence is unclear, the question is not answerable, or the options cannot be made sufficiently distinct.

评估员工作流程。Evaluator workflow.

验证工作流程如下：The verification workflow is as follows:

  1. 1.

    仅在需要时收听音频并查阅文字记录。Listen to the audio and consult the transcript only if needed.

  2. 2.

    判断标记的答案是否正确。Decide whether the labeled answer is correct.

  3. 3.

    如果正确，则将该实例标记为正确。If correct, mark the instance as correct.

  4. 4.

    如果不正确，请更新最终答案索引或修改一个答案选择。If incorrect, either update the final answer index or revise one answer choice.

  5. 5.

    检查所有答案选项是否清晰且可区分。Check that all answer choices are clear and distinguishable.

附录FAppendix F音频孪生表示详细信息Audio Twin Representation Details

本附录提供了第 5 节中使用的音频孪生表示的实现细节This appendix provides implementation details for the Audio Twin representation used in Section4.2。 音频孪生将语音衍生的证据存储为紧凑的 JSON 格式. The Audio Twin stores speech-derived evidence as compact JSON-like证据卡evidence cards具有稳定的标识符和固定的字段。 这些卡片的构建独立于下游问题，并且仅在推理期间被查询。with stable identifiers and fixed fields. These cards are constructed independently of the downstream question and are queried only during inference.

特征提取前端。Feature extraction front ends.我们使用耳语We use Whisper[Radford et al., 2023]获取带时间戳的转录本和回合级 ASR 片段。 使用 Parselmouth 提取低级韵律特征，包括响度、基频和音高变化to obtain timestamped transcripts and turn-level ASR segments. Low-level prosodic features, including loudness, fundamental frequency, and pitch variation, are extracted with Parselmouth[Jadoul et al., 2018]，Praat 的 Python 接口。 使用 Vox-Profile 估计更高级别的说话者和言语特征属性，包括说话者人口统计、流利度、效价、唤醒度、主导度和分类情感, a Python interface to Praat. Higher-level speaker and speech-trait attributes, including speaker demographics, fluency, valence, arousal, dominance, and categorical emotion, are estimated with Vox-Profile[Feng et al., 2025]。 这些前端提供与转录回合对齐并文本化为音频双证据卡的原始线索。. These front ends provide the raw cues that are aligned to transcript turns and textualized into Audio Twin evidence cards.

转动对齐。Turn alignment.

每个转录回合都使用时间戳重叠（如果可用）链接到其相应的声学片段。 当重叠覆盖至少一半的转录本轮持续时间时，时间戳对齐被分配为高可靠性；当存在正重叠但比例低于此阈值时，时间戳对齐被分配为中等可靠性。 当时间戳对齐不可用或不足时，系统会回退到转录本文本相似度，其最小相似度得分为Each transcript turn is linked to its corresponding acoustic segment using timestamp overlap when available. Timestamp alignment is assigned high reliability when the overlap covers at least half of the transcript-turn duration, and medium reliability when positive overlap exists but the ratio is below this threshold. When timestamp alignment is unavailable or insufficient, the system falls back to transcript-text similarity with a minimum similarity score of0.500.50。 如果这也失败，系统将使用同一发言者的轮流顺序并将证据标记为低可靠性。 如果没有可用的同一说话者片段，则对齐标记为缺失。. If this also fails, the system uses same-speaker turn order and marks the evidence as low reliability. If no same-speaker segment is available, the alignment is marked missing.

证据家庭。Evidence families.

音频孪生包含三个主要证据系列。The Audio Twin contains three main evidence families.

  • •

    翻牌。Turn cards.每张回合卡将一个转录本回合与对齐的语音衍生线索联系起来，包括响度、音调水平、音调变化、语速、停顿前、停顿后、重叠、效价、唤醒、主导、分类情感、情感置信度和流畅度。 它还存储对齐方法和可靠性。Each turn card links one transcript turn to aligned speech-derived cues, including loudness, pitch level, pitch variation, speaking rate, pause-before, pause-after, overlap, valence, arousal, dominance, categorical emotion, emotion confidence, and fluency. It also stores the alignment method and reliability.

  • •

    扬声器基线卡。Speaker baseline cards.这些卡片总结了每个说话者通常的响度、音调水平、音调变化、语速、情感概况和流畅度。 它们支持与说话者相关的解释，例如区分一般表达能力强的说话者和在特定回合中表达能力异常的说话者。 当至少有四个同一说话人的特征观察可用时，基线可靠性标记为高，否则标记为低。These cards summarize each speaker’s usual loudness, pitch level, pitch variation, speaking rate, affective profile, and fluency. They support speaker-relative interpretation, for example distinguishing generally expressive speakers from speakers who are unusually expressive in a specific turn. Baseline reliability is marked high when at least four same-speaker feature observations are available and low otherwise.

  • •

    对话动态卡。Dialogue-dynamics cards.这些卡片总结了交互级别的模式，例如轮次计数、发言时间、重叠计数、总重叠持续时间和最大重叠持续时间以及每个发言者的平均响应延迟模式。These cards summarize interaction-level patterns such as turn counts, speaking time, overlap count, total and maximum overlap duration, and mean response-delay patterns for each speaker.

当检索计划需要时，该实现还支持辅助证据记录。 本地窗口记录保留围绕目标线的附近转录本。上下文块将选定的行功能附加到本地窗口，并包含提醒模型在时间顺序上下文中解释目标行的注释。 代表回合卡检索发言者的高唤醒或高主导回合。 演讲者比较卡将两位演讲者的基线摘要放在同一个记录中，允许模型直接比较他们的典型演讲模式。 当说话者属性记录存在于特征文件中时，说话者属性记录与转弯级别声学证据分开存储。The implementation also supports auxiliary evidence records when required by the retrieval plan. Local window records preserve nearby transcript turns around a target line. Context blocks attach selected-line functions to the local window and include notes reminding the model to interpret the target line in chronological context. Representative-turn cards retrieve high-arousal or high-dominance turns for a speaker. Speaker-comparison cards place both speakers’ baseline summaries in the same record, allowing the model to compare their typical delivery patterns directly. Speaker-attribute records, when present in the feature files, are stored separately from turn-level acoustic evidence.

证据标识符。Evidence identifiers.

每个证据条目都有一个稳定的标识符。 转录锚点使用行标识符，例如Each evidence entry has a stable identifier. Transcript anchors use line identifiers such asL015。 转牌使用标识符，例如. Turn cards use identifiers such as卡_L015CARD_L015;本地窗口和上下文块使用; local windows and context blocks use窗口_L015WINDOW_L015和and上下文_L015CONTEXT_L015。 扬声器基线使用. Speaker baselines use基线_ABASELINE_A和and基线_BBASELINE_B，对话级证据使用标识符，例如, and dialogue-level evidence uses identifiers such as对话动态DIALOGUE_DYNAMICS和and总体比较COMPARISON_OVERALL.

特征文本化。Feature textualization.

连续的声学和计时特征在暴露给推理模型之前被转换为文本。 韵律和计时值是相对于同一说话者的分布进行编码的。 当至少有四个同一说话人的观察可用时，系统使用Continuous acoustic and timing features are converted into text before being exposed to the reasoning model. Prosodic and timing values are encoded relative to the same speaker’s distribution. When at least four same-speaker observations are available, the system uses azz-分数阈值-score threshold of±0.75\pm 0.75将值标记为低于平常、典型或高于平常。 当可用的观察值较少时，它会回退到与同一说话人的平均值进行比率比较：以下值to label a value as lower than usual, typical, or higher than usual. When fewer observations are available, it falls back to a ratio comparison against the same-speaker mean: values below0.75×0.75\times说话人的平均值被标记为低于平常，值高于平常the speaker mean are labeled lower than usual, values above1.25×1.25\times说话者平均值被标记为高于平常，并且介于两者之间的值被标记为典型值。the speaker mean are labeled higher than usual, and values in between are labeled typical.

情感分数在标准化模型输出尺度上使用固定阈值进行离散化。 对于化合价分数Affective scores are discretized with fixed thresholds on normalized model-output scales. For valence scores in the[0,1][0,1]范围，系统将值映射到range, the system maps values to非常消极very negative, 消极的negative, 中立的neutral, 积极的positive, 和, and非常积极very positive使用阈值using thresholds0.300.30, 0.450.45, 0.550.55, 和, and0.700.70。 对于唤醒度、支配力和情绪信心得分. For arousal, dominance, and emotion confidence scores in the[0,1][0,1]范围，系统使用阈值range, the system uses thresholds0.400.40和and0.700.70生产低、中、高标签。 分类情绪预测与效价、唤醒度和优势相结合，形成一个紧凑的情绪印象场。to produce low, medium, and high labels. Categorical emotion predictions are combined with valence, arousal, and dominance to form a compact emotion-impression field.

证据注释。Evidence notes.

转牌还包括简短的、源自规则的注释，描述声学证据支持什么、它与什么解释兼容，以及如果没有话语上下文就无法确定什么。 例如，高唤醒度支持高声音或情绪激活，而负价支持负面情绪。 这些注释还指出了局限性：真诚、社会意图、讽刺、敌意和信心需要对话背景，不能仅从低级声音线索中推断出来。 这些注释旨在使证据可用于推理，同时避免对声学特征的夸大。Turn cards additionally include short, rule-derived notes describing what the acoustic evidence supports, what interpretations it remains compatible with, and what it cannot establish without discourse context. For example, high arousal supports high vocal or emotional activation, while negative valence supports negative affect. The notes also state limitations: sincerity, social intent, sarcasm, hostility, and confidence require dialogue context and cannot be inferred from low-level acoustic cues alone. These notes are intended to make the evidence usable for reasoning while avoiding overclaiming from acoustic features.

信息隔离。Information isolation.

音频双胞胎仅由转录和音频衍生功能构建。 它不包括黄金答案、演讲者提示、构建时间标签、人工验证决策或问题生成解释。 模型可见问题对象仅包含问题文本、四个候选答案和问题类别。 因此，该表示提供了语音传递的文本界面，而不是基准标签的快捷方式。The Audio Twin is built from the transcript and audio-derived features only. It does not include gold answers, speaker prompts, construction-time labels, human-verification decisions, or question-generation explanations. The model-visible question object contains only the question text, four answer candidates, and the question category. Thus, the representation provides a textual interface to speech delivery rather than a shortcut to the benchmark labels.

附录GAppendix G代理式证据检索细节Agentic-style Evidence Retrieval Details

本附录提供了第 5 节中描述的代理式证据检索程序的实施细节。This appendix provides implementation details for the agentic-style evidence retrieval procedure described in Section4.3。 给出一个问题. Given a questionqq，回答候选人, answer candidatesC={c1,…,c4}C=\{c_{1},\ldots,c_{4}\}和目标话语维度，系统首先构建一个证据计划，确定在答案预测之前应该检索哪些证据。, and the target discourse dimension, the system first constructs an evidence plan that determines what evidence should be retrieved before answer prediction.

证据计划作业。Evidence-plan assignment.

对于评估的目标维度，证据计划分配是确定性的。 针对情绪状态的问题分配给For the evaluated target dimensions, evidence-plan assignment is deterministic. Questions targeting emotion state are assigned to情绪状态emotion state;针对交互行为的问题被分配给; questions targeting interaction behavior are assigned to交互行为interaction behavior;社会立场和对话意图问题被分配给; social-stance and conversational-intent questions are assigned to扬声器级风格speaker-level style;对话行为问题被分配给; and dialogue-act questions are assigned to当地韵律传递local prosodic delivery。 需要比较演讲者（包括人口统计选择线索）的问题或答案候选人被分配给. Questions or answer candidates that require comparing speakers, including demographic-choice cues, are assigned to扬声器比较speaker comparison。 该模型可能会提出额外的证据来检查，但它不能覆盖基于规则的证据计划类型。. The model may propose additional evidence to inspect, but it cannot override the rule-based evidence-plan type.

证据计划类型。Evidence-plan types.

我们使用五种证据计划类型，每种类型对应于回答问题所需的不同类型的语音证据。We use five evidence-plan types, each corresponding to a different kind of speech evidence needed for answering the question.

  • •

    情绪状态。Emotion state.检索局部情感线索，例如目标话语和附近上下文的效价、唤醒度、主导度、分类情感预测以及情感置信度。Retrieves local affective cues such as valence, arousal, dominance, categorical emotion predictions, and emotion confidence for the target utterance and nearby context.

  • •

    交互行为。Interaction behavior.检索轮流证据，例如暂停、重叠、响应延迟、类似中断的行为、相邻轮流和对话级动态。Retrieves turn-taking evidence such as pauses, overlap, response delays, interruption-like behavior, neighboring turns, and dialogue-level dynamics.

  • •

    扬声器级风格。Speaker-level style.检索与说话者相关的表达模式，包括对话中的韵律、强度、流畅度和重复的与立场相关的线索。Retrieves speaker-relative delivery patterns, including prosody, intensity, fluency, and repeated stance-related cues across the dialogue.

  • •

    本地韵律传递。Local prosodic delivery.检索目标话语相对于其本地上下文和同一说话者基线的音调、响度、时间和强度提示。Retrieves the target utterance’s pitch, loudness, timing, and intensity cues relative to its local context and the same speaker’s baseline.

  • •

    扬声器比较。Speaker comparison.检索对比两位演讲者的表达方式、情感模式、演讲者基线或对话行为的对比证据。Retrieves contrastive evidence comparing the two speakers’ delivery, affective patterns, speaker baselines, or dialogue behavior.

锚点选择策略。Anchor selection policy.

每个证据计划类型指定在检索之前应选择多少个转录锚点。 对于Each evidence-plan type specifies how many transcript anchors should be selected before retrieval. For情绪状态emotion state, 扬声器级风格speaker-level style, 和, and当地韵律传递local prosodic delivery，系统选择三到六个转录本行。 对于, the system selects three to six transcript lines. For交互行为interaction behavior和and扬声器比较speaker comparison，它选择四到六个转录本行。 所有计划至少需要一个, it selects four to six transcript lines. All plans require at least one主要目标primary target线和周围的上下文证据。 对于说话者比较计划，检索包括来自两个说话者的对比证据，并且如果缺少所需的说话者证据，则验证将证据包标记为不完整。line and surrounding contextual evidence. For speaker-comparison plans, retrieval includes contrastive evidence from both speakers, and validation marks the evidence bundle incomplete if the required speaker evidence is missing.

转录本地化。Transcript localization.

完整转录本定位器使用行编号的转录本、问题和答案候选者来选择相关的转录本锚点。 定位器仅限于识别证据位置。它不会选择答案或评估答案选项。 对于每条选定的台词，系统都会记录该台词在以后的推理中应如何使用：作为目标话语、周围上下文、同一说话者比较、其他说话者响应或对比证据。A full-transcript locator uses the line-numbered transcript, question, and answer candidates to select relevant transcript anchors. The locator is constrained to identify evidence locations only. It does not choose an answer or evaluate the answer options. For each selected line, the system records how the line should be used in later reasoning: as the target utterance, surrounding context, same-speaker comparison, other-speaker response, or contrastive evidence.

定位器标准化和修复。Locator normalization and repair.

在检索之前，系统将定位器输出转换为一组有效的转录锚点。 每个选定的行都会转换为内部标识符格式Before retrieval, the system converts the locator output into a valid set of transcript anchors. Each selected line is converted to the internal identifier formatL###（例如，数字定位器输出为(for example, a numeric locator output of15被转换为is converted toL015）。 不对应于任何转录行的选择将被删除，除非可以通过匹配问题中引用的短语来恢复它们。 重复的行选择被合并。). Selections that do not correspond to any transcript line are removed unless they can be recovered by matching a quoted phrase from the question. Duplicate line selections are merged.

如果定位器选择的台词多于证据计划允许的台词，系统首先保留最重要的台词：目标话语、问题中引用的台词、直接相邻的上下文、同一说话者的比较台词和对比证据。 如果定位器错过了所需的目标行、选择了太少的有效行、选择了大部分无效的行标识符，或者未能包含问题中明确引用的行，则会发出修复提示。 如果修复仍然失败，系统会选择与问题文本相似度最高的转录行，并使用附近的上下文行扩展证据集。If the locator selects more lines than allowed by the evidence plan, the system keeps the most important lines first: target utterances, quoted lines from the question, immediate neighboring context, same-speaker comparison lines, and contrastive evidence. If the locator misses a required target line, selects too few valid lines, selects mostly invalid line identifiers, or fails to include a line explicitly quoted in the question, a repair prompt is issued. If repair still fails, the system selects the transcript line with the highest text similarity to the question and expands the evidence set with nearby context lines.

证据规划和检索。Evidence planning and retrieval.

给定选定的锚点，系统确定分配的证据计划类型需要哪些音频孪生条目。 此步骤仅使用选定的转录本行而不是完整的转录本，使后续推理集中于本地证据。 一旦确定了锚点和证据计划，检索就具有确定性。 系统获取选定的转录回合、对齐的回合卡、说话者基线卡和本地上下文块。 根据证据计划类型，它还可以检索本地窗口卡、对话动态卡、说话者比较卡、代表回合卡或说话者属性记录。Given the selected anchors, the system determines which Audio Twin entries are needed for the assigned evidence-plan type. This step uses only the selected transcript lines rather than the full transcript, keeping later reasoning focused on localized evidence. Once the anchors and evidence plan are fixed, retrieval is deterministic. The system fetches the selected transcript turns, aligned turn cards, speaker baseline cards, and local context blocks. Depending on the evidence-plan type, it may also retrieve local window cards, dialogue-dynamics cards, speaker-comparison cards, representative-turn cards, or speaker-attribute records.

对于每个主要目标行，系统按照时间顺序从附近的转录本构建本地上下文块。 该块保留相邻的转弯，记录每条选定的线在推理中的使用方式，并总结目标是否出现在来回交换中或较长的同一说话者延伸中。 当说话者之间反复交替附近的转弯时，就可以识别出来回交换，这可以指示交互时间，例如快速响应、中断或立即反应。 当附近的转弯大部分来自同一说话者时，该块被视为同一说话者延续，这对于解释相对于该说话者周围语音的目标线更有用。For each primary target line, the system constructs a local context block from nearby transcript turns in chronological order. The block keeps the neighboring turns, records how each selected line is used in reasoning, and summarizes whether the target occurs in a back-and-forth exchange or within a longer same-speaker stretch. A back-and-forth exchange is identified when nearby turns alternate repeatedly between speakers, which can indicate interactional timing such as quick responses, interruptions, or immediate reactions. When the nearby turns are mostly from the same speaker, the block is treated as same-speaker continuation, which is more useful for interpreting the target line relative to that speaker’s surrounding speech.

证据验证。Evidence validation.

在答案预测之前，系统会检查检索到的证据是否满足证据计划。 验证验证所选锚点是否满足所需的行数、包括主要目标、包含所需的上下文，并与来自正确转录行和扬声器的音频孪生条目配对。 对于情绪状态、说话者级别风格和本地韵律传递计划，所需的证据包括目标转录轮次、对齐的轮次卡和相应的说话者基线。 对于交互行为计划，它包括文字交换证据和对话动态证据。 对于演讲者比较计划，它包括来自两位演讲者的证据、演讲者比较卡和代表回合卡。Before answer prediction, the system checks whether the retrieved evidence satisfies the evidence plan. Validation verifies that the selected anchors meet the required line count, include a primary target, contain required context, and are paired with Audio Twin entries from the correct transcript lines and speakers. For emotion-state, speaker-level-style, and local-prosodic-delivery plans, the required evidence includes a target transcript turn, an aligned turn card, and the corresponding speaker baseline. For interaction-behavior plans, it includes transcript-exchange evidence and dialogue-dynamics evidence. For speaker-comparison plans, it includes evidence from both speakers, a speaker-comparison card, and representative-turn cards.

如果缺少任何所需的证据，则证据包将被标记为不完整，并记录缺少的证据类型。 管道可能仍会产生强制的多项选择答案，但运行会被标记为不完整的检索，并且可以通过跟踪和输出字段进行审核。 因此，单独选择转录本行并不被视为成功检索。所选线路必须与所需的音频双证据配对。If any required evidence is missing, the evidence bundle is marked incomplete and the missing evidence type is recorded. The pipeline may still produce a forced multiple-choice answer, but the run is flagged with incomplete retrieval and is auditable through the trace and output fields. Thus, selecting transcript lines alone is not treated as successful retrieval. The selected lines must be paired with the required Audio Twin evidence.

提示界限。Prompt boundaries.

完整的行编号转录本仅暴露给转录本定位器。 证据规划步骤接收选定的线路和检查需求，而不是完整的成绩单。 诊断基础步骤接收经过验证的检索包和系统验证结果。 应答阶段接收诊断基础结果和一组经过验证的证据标识符。 这种分离可以防止后期阶段在检索后引入新的转录本区域。The full line-numbered transcript is exposed only to the transcript locator. The evidence-planning step receives the selected lines and inspection needs, not the full transcript. The diagnostic-grounding step receives the validated retrieval bundle and system validation result. The answer stage receives the diagnostic grounding result and the set of validated evidence identifiers. This separation prevents later stages from introducing new transcript regions after retrieval.

阶段验证。Stage validation.

每个模型调用都会根据预期的输出格式进行检查，然后再将其结果供下一阶段使用。 定位器输出必须包含转录行选择及其预期用途，但不包含答案预测。 如果它包含类似答案的字段，例如选择索引、最终答案、候选比较或选择级别支持，则会被拒绝。 证据规划输出必须仅指定检索需求，并且如果它尝试选择答案或提供纯文本首选项，则会被拒绝。 诊断基础输出必须包括最终候选者、候选者级别的证据评估以及表面转录读数不足的原因的解释。 答案输出必须包含有效的从零开始的选择索引，并且任何引用的证据都必须来自经过验证的检索包。Each model call is checked against an expected output format before its result is used by the next stage. The locator output must contain transcript-line selections and their intended uses, but no answer prediction. It is rejected if it includes answer-like fields such as a choice index, final answer, candidate comparison, or choice-level support. The evidence-planning output must specify retrieval needs only, and is rejected if it attempts to choose an answer or provide a text-only preference. The diagnostic-grounding output must include a final candidate, candidate-level evidence assessments, and an explanation of why the surface transcript reading is insufficient. The answer output must contain a valid zero-based choice index, and any cited evidence must come from the validated retrieval bundle.

诊断接地。Diagnostic grounding.

最后的推理步骤从四个角度比较检索到的证据：目标话语本身、周围的对话上下文、从音频孪生检索到的声学证据以及支持或反对每个候选答案的证据。 对于每个候选者，该模型记录了该候选者正确所需的条件、文字记录是否支持它、本地上下文是否支持它、声学证据是否支持它以及是否有任何证据与之相矛盾。 然后将选择的候选证据分类为The final reasoning step compares the retrieved evidence from four perspectives: the target utterance by itself, the surrounding dialogue context, the acoustic evidence retrieved from the Audio Twin, and the evidence for or against each answer candidate. For each candidate, the model records what would need to be true for that candidate to be correct, whether the transcript supports it, whether the local context supports it, whether the acoustic evidence supports it, and whether any evidence contradicts it. The choice candidate evidence is then classified as诊断diagnostic, 兼容但不具有诊断性compatible but not diagnostic, 矛盾的contradictory, 或, or不足insufficient。 最终答案是从该诊断基础结果中选择的，任何引用的证据都必须来自经过验证的检索包。. The final answer is selected from this diagnostic grounding result, and any cited evidence must come from the validated retrieval bundle.

执行痕迹。Execution traces.

每次运行都会存储一个 JSON 跟踪，其中包含审计管道所需的中间输出：定位器输出、证据计划、检索到的证据标识符、检索验证结果、证据包、诊断基础输出、最终答案输出和验证错误。 表格输出记录证据计划类型、计划是否满足、缺失证据、声学证据计数、检索状态、接地状态、答案解析状态、证据引用状态以及跟踪文件的路径。 这些字段可以识别错误是否来自本地化、检索、证据验证、基础、答案解析或验证包之外的证据引用。Each run stores a JSON trace with the intermediate outputs needed to audit the pipeline: the locator output, evidence plan, retrieved evidence identifiers, retrieval validation result, evidence bundle, diagnostic-grounding output, final answer output, and validation errors. The tabular output records the evidence-plan type, whether the plan was satisfied, missing evidence, acoustic evidence count, retrieval status, grounding status, answer-parsing status, evidence-citation status, and the path to the trace file. These fields make it possible to identify whether an error came from localization, retrieval, evidence validation, grounding, answer parsing, or citation of evidence outside the validated bundle.

证据规划输出将实例分配给The evidence-planning output assigns the instance to the交互行为interaction_behavior在检索之前计划并防止答案选择。存储的计划包括：plan and prevents answer selection before retrieval. The stored plan includes:

诊断接地。Diagnostic grounding.

诊断基础输出将纯文本表面阅读与本地对话上下文和检索到的声学证据进行比较。孤立的目标首先被认为具有潜在的误导性：The diagnostic-grounding output compares the text-only surface reading with the local dialogue context and the retrieved acoustic evidence. The isolated target is first recognized as potentially misleading:

“‘嗯嗯’单独读起来是一个中性的继续/监听标记。”“’Mm-hmm’ in isolation reads as a neutral continuer/listening token.”

然后，本地上下文的解读将解释转向选择 0：The local-context reading then shifts the interpretation toward choice 0:

“L026 is followed by disfluent topic-shift markers: ’Oh, oh, okay’ (L027), ’Is, is, yeah, I’m so sorry’ (L028), before finally raising the noise complaint (L029). The backchannel sits at a hinge point where B is preparing to abandon A’s family topic and introduce a face-threatening complaint, suggesting it functions as a stalling/bracing token rather than routine listenership.”

The trace explicitly records the conflict between the transcript-plausible surface reading and the audio-grounded answer:

“Read alone, ’Mm-hmm’ looks like a generic neutral continuer (choice 3). But acoustic marking (slower, stretched, pitch-varied, lowered loudness vs. B’s baseline and vs. her earlier neutral L021 backchannel) plus the immediately following disfluent restarts and topic pivot to a complaint show the token is functioning as a hesitation/bracing device before a difficult topic shift.”

The diagnostic step records text_only_trap_or_surface_reading: 3, final_candidate: 0, and text_alone_sufficient: false.

Answer.

The final answer output selects choice 0. The stored response is:

“L026’s ’Mm-hmm’ is prosodically marked (stretched ∼\sim2.46s, slower, lowered loudness, higher and more varied pitch) compared to B’s baseline and her earlier neutral backchannel at L021. It is immediately followed by disfluent restarts (’Oh, oh, okay’; ’Is, is, yeah, I’m so sorry’) before B introduces the face-threatening noise complaint, indicating the token functions as a stalling/bracing device rather than a neutral continuer or smooth transition.”

The predicted answer is therefore:

Choice 0: Buying time and steeling herself for the topic shift.

This example shows a conflict case where the transcript-plausible answer is rejected after speaker-relative acoustic evidence and local sequential context are retrieved.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
